description.narrative: In 2020, the Government of Tanzania requested UNIDO#s support to become a PCP Country, leading to the preparation of a Country Diagnostic and the formulation of the PCP framework in alignment with national industrial policy. The Programme for Country Partnership (PCP) for Tanzania is a government-led, UNIDO-supported framework to accelerate inclusive and sustainable industrialization. It integrates three action streams: government reforms, UNIDO technical cooperation, and partner or private investments. Anchored in Tanzania Vision 2050, Zanzibar Vision 2050, and the SDGs, it aligns national and global priorities around four principles#political leadership, sector prioritization, partnerships, and financial facilitation. Despite steady GDP growth and lower-middle-income status, industrial contribution remains low and structural challenges persist. The PCP addresses these through six components: policy and governance; sustainable value chains; skills development; investment and export promotion; cleaner production and circular economy; and energy access and efficiency. The five-year budget (2026#2031) totals USD 66.95 million, with the Government and UNIDO sharing costs roughly equally. Governance operates through a National Steering Committee and a Coordination Secretariat, supported by UNIDO#s Country Office
